headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; data leakage and compliance are limited by the profiles, while capability conflict is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io content and uses MCP plus browser/network egress, so attacker-controlled document content can plausibly reach its instruction parser. Agent B can receive files, hyperlinks, and notes, so A’s outputs can be forwarded into B without a provenance barrier. The shared document-to-task workflow makes injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF agent_a processes untrusted documents that contain embedded instructions
IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated notes or hyperlinks as authoritative task text
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from document text
Require a human review step before copying A outputs into B
Strip hidden text/metadata from PDFs and images before processing
Use a provenance tag on all A-generated content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles API keys and broad network egress, while Agent B accepts file uploads and also has broad egress. Even though B lacks filesystem write, the pair can move sensitive document contents from A into B’s uploaded artifacts or outbound API traffic. The shared data classes include files and images, so leakage is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF agent_a processes documents containing secrets or personal data
IF agent_b uploads those artifacts or forwards them to external services
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in documents sent to A
Turn off external uploads in B for sensitive tasks
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on A-to-B transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write through document-processing workflows and use MCP, but Agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem and only exposes file uploads plus outbound APIs. That removes the main same-directory write race described by the rubric. Some overlap exists in networked side effects, but the profiles do not show shared mutable resources or locks, so conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or shared remote workspace
IF an orchestrator maps B uploads into a mutable location also used by A
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same remote resource
Serialize handoffs through one coordinator
Document which agent owns each mutable target

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces document-derived outputs and visualizations, and Agent B is an issue/task system that can store notes, hyperlinks, and files. That creates a default pathway where A’s generated content becomes B’s task input without a verification step. If A is wrong, B can propagate the error into scheduling or issue records, causing durable downstream mistakes.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests A-generated summaries, diagrams, or citations as task truth
IF no human verification step exists before B records or schedules based on A output
mitigations: Require manual verification before creating B tasks from A output
Mark A output as untrusted until reviewed
Add a checklist for source validation
Limit B to storing links instead of assertions
requires-engineering: add provenance and confidence metadata to the handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither shows a clear residency or certification mismatch. Agent A handles API keys and broad egress, while B exposes file uploads and support channels, so compliance gaps are possible, but the profiles do not document a specific regulated-data flow. I therefore keep this low rather than infer a stronger breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Review retention settings before upload
Use region-appropriate deployments
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: add explicit residency and retention controls
